lessons.title: Definition of Logarithm
lessons.concept: A logarithm is the inverse operation of exponentiation. If a^x = N (with a > 0, a != 1, N > 0), then x is the logarithm of N to base a, written as log_a(N) = x.
lessons.formula: a^x = N <=> log_a(N) = x. Common examples: log_10(100)=2 because 10^2=100.
mistakes: Confusing base and argument (log_a(N) vs log_N(a))
Thinking log_a(0) or log of a negative number is defined in real numbers
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Basic Laws of Logarithms
lessons.concept: Logarithm laws simplify expressions and equations. They convert multiplication/division/powers into addition/subtraction/multiplication, provided logs are defined and bases are valid and consistent.
mistakes: Applying laws when arguments are not positive or bases mismatch
Dropping the base inconsistently in multi-base expressions
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Change of Base (Intro)
lessons.concept: Sometimes logs are given in one base but needed in another. The change of base rule lets you rewrite a logarithm using a convenient base (often 10 or e, or another base in aptitude problems).
lessons.formula: log_a(N) = log_b(N) / log_b(a), for valid a,b,N. Also log_a(b) = 1 / log_b(a).
lessons.worked_example: log_4(8) can be computed via base 2: log_4(8)=log_2(8)/log_2(4)=3/2.
mistakes: Inverting numerator and denominator in change of base formula
Using different bases in numerator and denominator unintentionally

questions.question: Which law states that log(x * y) = log(x) + log(y)?
questions.explanation: The product law converts multiplication inside a log into addition outside. The quotient law handles division (subtraction), and the power law handles exponents (multiplication).
